item.title: SplashBI opens GCC in Hyderabad, to invest over $100M
item.description:
The investment to be spread across 5 years
The GCC of SplashBI will strengthen the company’s product engineering and delivery capabilities
SplashBI, a Georgia (US)-headquartered enterprise data intelligence platform, opened its global capability centre (GCC) in Hyderabad.
The company plans to i
item.content:encoded:
SplashBI, a Georgia (US)-headquartered enterprise data intelligence platform, has opened its global capability centre (GCC) in Hyderabad.

The company plans to invest over $100 million over the next five to seven years in infrastructure, technology and talent to scale the Hyderabad centre and strengthen its global product engineering and delivery capabilities, a release said.

The 20,000-square-foot facility, with capacity for 275 professionals, was inaugurated by Telangana IT Minister D Sridhar Babu.

SplashBI has had a presence in Hyderabad since 2014. The new facility brings its teams in the city together under one roof, designed to support collaboration and growth, the release said.

The centre will support the development of SplashBI’s data intelligence platform and global customer delivery, helping enterprises connect business data, establish shared business context and use that data for decisions, AI, analytics and reporting, it said.

Platform engineering, AI development, domain analytics and customer delivery teams will work closely together at the Global Capability Center, the release said.

They will work on data connectivity and business modelling, develop SplashAI capabilities and support customer implementations.

“Enterprises need a practical way to turn the data they already have into decisions they can trust. That requires understanding how their business works, connecting information across functions and giving people useful ways to explore it,” said Naveen Miglani, CEO and Co-Founder of SplashBI.

“Our Hyderabad centre strengthens the engineering and customer expertise behind that work, as we help customers advance their data foundations and adopt AI with the right business context,” he added.

Kiran Reddy Pasham, President and Co-Founder of SplashBI, said, “Our teams in Hyderabad will build the platform capabilities and domain content that help customers connect their data, make sense of it and use it in their everyday work.”

item.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 6, 2026)
item.description: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Friday, November 06, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
From Deepinder Goyal defending wearable device Temple to xxx raising Rs 400 crore, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.

Featured news

How Satin Group’s Sankalp plans to empower Indian founders

Satin Group launched Sankalp this September, a platform designed to nurture sustainability-focused ideas from students and early-stage entrepreneurs. In an exclusive interaction with YourStory, Pramod Marar, CEO of Satin FinServ Limited, discussed the thinking behind the initiative, the importance of non-financial support alongside funding, and the role financial institutions can play in scaling climate innovation.     

Sankalp operates through two distinct tracks: student-led business ideas and early-stage startups. The student track encourages college students to develop technology-driven solutions to climate and environmental challenges. The startup track focuses on young businesses working in areas such as clean mobility, circular economy, waste management, and sustainable supply chains. Sankalp winners stand a chance to win Rs 32 lakh, with Rs 10 lakh for students and Rs 22 lakh for startups.

Read More

Latest news

Deepinder Goyal hits back at doctors

Deepinder Goyal took to X on Thursday to counter Indian doctors who criticised his brain-monitoring wearable Temple. Defending the science behind the device, he said, “First and foremost, a business lesson: if Temple were a scam, and any of what we said weren't true, people would know it in just a few days of using Temple.”

He also said the device features a 14-day no-question return policy. “If the product doesn't work, it fails out of the gate and the company dies before recovering a tenth of its R&D," he said.

In the post, Goyal also highlighted that $30 million was invested in building the device, of which he put in $20 million of his personal money.

Funding news

Northern Arc hits first close at over Rs 400 crore

Northern Arc Investment Managers, the asset management arm of Northern Arc Capital, has marked the first close of its Northern Arc Diversified Debt Fund with commitments of more than Rs 400 crore from institutions, family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) and high-net-worth individuals (HNIs).

The fund is the firm's 15th private credit vehicle. It is a sector-agnostic Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) focused on performing private credit, rated AA (SO) by CareEdge Ratings. It targets a corpus of Rs 1,500 crore, with a greenshoe option of Rs 500 crore that could take it to Rs 2,000 crore. The fund has a five-year tenure and targets a 16% XIRR.

Read More

Fitness and sports technology startup OBSESS raises angel funding

Delhi NCR-based fitness and sports technology company OBSESS has raised angel funding to build a unified digital ecosystem for India’s fitness and sports industry. The round saw participation from Angel Investors including Pushpendra Singh, Co-founder of Centricity; Amitt Goel, Angel Investor; and Harshit Vij, Co-founder of Freecultr.

Founded in 2026 by Tushar Sharma and Yash Kumar, OBSESS brings different parts of the fitness journey together through a single connected platform.

(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

item.title: (Weekly funding roundup Oct 31-Nov 6) Sharp rise in capital inflow
item.description: The total funding for the first week of November was $263 million across 23 deals, compared to just $115 million in the previous week.
item.content:encoded:
November began on a positive note for the Indian startup ecosystem with venture capital funding seeing a sharp rise, after four weeks of tepid inflow of funds.

The total funding for the first week of November was $263 million across 23 deals, compared to just $115 million in the previous week.

This week saw two key breakthroughs.

First, the total funding amount was well above $200 million. This is significant as the funds raised in the preceding four weeks were below $200 million. Second, after four weeks, the Indian startup ecosystem saw a $100-million transaction from jewellery brand GIVA.

These developments provide a big boost to the startup ecosystem, which has been struggling to raise large amounts of capital. Additionally, a potential investor slump in AI companies in the aftermath of the US mid-term elections could benefit Indian startups.

This is because much of the money is concentrated in the AI segment in the US. Now one can expect some sort of rebalancing in capital distribution with certain funds flowing into India. However, it is early days to comment on how the capital will flow into the country.

Key transactions

Jewellery brand GIVA raised $100 million led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management.

Consumer AI startup EloElo Group raised $80 million from Hornbill Capital, NBCUniversal, MIT Investment Co, Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures and Griffin Gaming Partners.

Healthtech startup Clinics On Cloud raised $12.5 million from Model42.

Peppermint Robotics raised Rs 100 crore (~$10.5 million) from pi Ventures, Crane Venture Partners and Asiana Fund.

Speciality chemicals startup altM raised $10.3 million from Rainmatter by Zerodha, Mela Ventures, Omnivore, Theia Ventures, Aureolis Ventures and Spectrum Impact.

Cleantech startup Two Point O Capital (TW.O) raised $10 million from Transition Venture Capital, Omnivore and angel investors.

Wealthtech startup PowerUp Money raised $10 million from Flourish Ventures, Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC.

Spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space raised $6 million from Rebright Partners, Aranya Holdings, Naandi Ventures, AUM Ventures and Shakti VC.

item.title: MakeMyTrip's India arm gets Sebi nod to float IPO
item.description:
MakeMyTrip is listed on Nasdaq stock exchange
The proceeds from the planned IPO will be utilised by MakeMyTrip for long term growth, inorganic opportunities and repurchase of different types shares
Nasdaq-listed travel booking platform MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary has received Sebi's approval to
item.content:encoded:
Nasdaq-listed travel booking platform MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary has received Sebi's approval to launch an initial public offering (IPO), according to an update available on the markets regulator's website.

MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd (MMT India) had filed draft papers with Sebi in July through the confidential route. After examining the draft documents, the regulator issued its final observations on November 6.

Sebi's observations mark an important step in the IPO process, allowing the company to proceed with preparations for its public issues, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.

The proposed IPO is expected to comprise a sale of equity shares in MMT India by its parent MakeMyTrip and its wholly-owned subsidiary, ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) Pte Ltd, the Gurugram-headquartered company said in a regulatory filing with Nasdaq.

Following the completion of the proposed IPO, MMT India will continue to remain a subsidiary of MakeMyTrip, with its financial results continuing to be consolidated with those of the parent company, it had said.

"MakeMyTrip expects the proposed initial public offering and listing of MMT India to enhance its brand visibility and support MMT India's ability to incentivise and promote talent in a competitive technology recruitment landscape," the filing stated.

The net proceeds received by MakeMyTrip and ibibo Group Holdings from the sale of shares in MMT India are expected to strengthen the parent's cash position.

The proceeds will be utilised for long-term growth, strategic inorganic initiatives and repurchases of different classes of securities, including convertible securities, by MakeMyTrip, the filing stated.

MakeMyTrip swung back into profit for the three months ending September, 2026 boosted by increased booking across all categories. The company reported a net profit of $1.8 million for the second quarter of FY27 as compared to loss of $5.7 million in the similar period a year ago. The revenue for the second quarter touched $235.2 million which was a 11.2% increase when compared to the similar period of last fiscal.

item.title: Nvidia probes whether foreign intelligence targeted Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company has said its board had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security had been compromised.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Readers,

Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The move follows a New York Times report alleging that a business executive with whom Huang had a close relationship passed information to Beijing.

The company shares slid sharply on Monday following this news. 

Nvidia said its board had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security had been compromised.

In other news, Sashikumar Sreedharan, the former MD for India at Google Cloud, has joined AI company Sarvam as President and Chief Business Officer. He will also be on the company’s board. Sreedharan will run Sarvam’s business across enterprises and government and expand its work with digital-native companies, developers and partners.

Meanwhile, the India subsidiary of travel booking platform MakeMyTrip has received Sebi’s approval to launch an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO is expected to comprise a sale of equity shares in MMT India by its parent MakeMyTrip and its wholly-owned subsidiary, ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) Pte Ltd. 

Lastly, 2026 is on track to be one of the four warmest years on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization.

In today’s newsletter, we will talk about 

  • How Bariflo uses AI to help factories treat wastewater
  • How these Mothers of Courage are fighting to keep girls in school

Here’s your trivia for today: What was Henry Ford’s original design for a car called? (Scroll down for the answer)

In-focus

How Bariflo uses AI to help factories treat wastewater

Bariflo Cybernetics wants factories to get more use out of their wastewater treatment plants. The Odisha-based startup combines sensors, AI software, and automation to adjust treatment processes, aiming to reduce the energy and chemicals needed to clean water for reuse. 

It recently secured Rs 2 crore in milestone-linked funding from energy innovation platform MC² Plus, an initiative led by the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, and is preparing for a pilot with Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), according to founder and CEO Mrityunjay Sahu. The funding comes as Bariflo moves from developing and testing its technology towards commercial deployments. That means persuading industrial customers to invest in upgrades that promise lower operating costs.

Key takeaways 

  • Founded in 2018, Bariflo initially focused on monitoring and cleaning municipal waterbodies. It subsequently explored aquaculture, including shrimp and fish farming, before concentrating on industrial wastewater treatment and reuse. It is now engaged in making existing treatment infrastructure smarter and more efficient. 
  • Bariflo’s proprietary IoT sensors monitor wastewater parameters such as pH, total dissolved solids, and flow. Its AI models use the readings to determine chemical dosage and treatment processes at different stages. This automates some decisions that operators would otherwise make manually and helps plants respond as the characteristics of incoming wastewater change. 
  • The company has conducted pilots with Indian Oil Corporation’s R&D centre in Faridabad. Its planned BPCL pilot will test treatment efficiency, energy consumption, and chemical use in an industrial setting. Founder Sahu hopes successful validation will pave the way for a commercial work order. 

Social impact

How these Mothers of Courage are fighting to keep girls in school 

Mothers of Courage, a documentary on girls’ education in Bihar, recently won the 2026 UN SDG Action Award in the Creativity category. It captures how women in rural Bihar are challenging social norms to keep girls in school.

Directed by Vandana R Jaikumar and produced by Butterfly Effect Media, the documentary was chosen from more than 7,000 applications from 190 countries and territories. 

Key takeaways 

  • In rural Bihar, mothers are at the centre of a quiet revolution. They are negotiating with their families so their daughters can keep studying. Others are standing up for daughters-in-law who want to return to school. This quiet, stubborn conviction and resilience is the subject of the documentary.
  • Mothers of Courage is part of Shikshagraha, a national movement to strengthen public education championed by Infosys Co-founder and former CEO S D Shibulal, and supported by Bengaluru-based non-profits ShikshaLokam and Mantra4Change.
  • Urmila Kumari, State Head for Shikshagraha in Bihar, is the living embodiment of the movement. She has spent nearly three decades working for the rights and education of girls and young women. She says the UN recognition belongs to “thousands of women and adolescent girls whose courage and determination have driven the fight for girls' education and rights.”

News & updates

  • New GCC: SplashBI, a Georgia (US)-headquartered enterprise data intelligence platform, has opened its global capability centre in Hyderabad. The company plans to invest over $100 million over five to seven years in infrastructure, technology and talent to scale the Hyderabad centre and strengthen its global product engineering and delivery capabilities. 
  • Age checks: Meta Platforms plans to expand its AI age-estimation technology globally to move millions more teens on Instagram ​into Teen Account protections, even if they have given ‌birth dates showing they are adults. This comes as the company faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young users.
  • AI guardrails: US President Donald Trump said the ​risks posed by artificial intelligence ‌can be managed but signalled an openness to safeguards, telling CBS’s 60 Minutes ​that he “doesn’t mind guardrails.”

What was Henry Ford’s original design for a car called?

Answer: Quadricycle

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits affair amid Chinese spying allegations; board launches probe
item.description: The AI chipmaker says it has no reason to believe company secrets were compromised, even as US lawmakers seek answers over potential national security risks.
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into reports that its founder and CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation, following his admission of an extramarital affair with a business executive whom US intelligence officials reportedly suspect of passing information to Beijing.

The development has raised questions about corporate security and the potential exposure of sensitive information at the world's most valuable company, whose advanced chips are central to the global artificial intelligence race.

In a letter to employees obtained by multiple news organisations, Huang, 63, acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and colleagues. He said he took full responsibility for his actions. "Leading Nvidia is the privilege of my life," Huang wrote. "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility."

Nvidia's board announced on Sunday that it would examine reports suggesting Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The investigation will be overseen by a committee of independent directors, assisted by external legal counsel. The board said it had no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia's confidential information had been compromised. However, it said the inquiry would review all available information.

Huang has agreed to cooperate with the investigation and will continue serving as CEO. "Today's news will not slow Nvidia," company spokesperson John Rizzo said in a statement, adding that Huang remained committed to leading the company without interruption.

Who is Alice Huang?

The investigation follows a report by The New York Times in October that US intelligence agencies had identified a close relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and business executive who allegedly supplied information to Beijing. The two are not related. Alice Huang, a former television reporter in China, subsequently became a senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, a major purchaser of Nvidia's AI chips.

According to The New York Times, Megaspeed purchased more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years. US authorities have also scrutinised Megaspeed over suspicions that it helped China obtain advanced AI processors subject to American export restrictions. The allegations involving Alice Huang have not been established by Nvidia's investigation, and the company has not reported evidence that its confidential information was compromised.

US lawmakers seek answers

The controversy has drawn attention from senior lawmakers in Washington, with three Republican congressional committee chairs seeking a closed-door briefing from Huang. In a letter dated November 4, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar and House Intelligence Committee Chairman Eric Crawford asked Huang to provide a briefing on November 18, according to Reuters.

The lawmakers raised concerns about whether the alleged intelligence operation could have exposed sensitive American technology or information to China. Nvidia previously said Huang interacts with thousands of customer executives annually and that its cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information rather than sensitive trade secrets or information connected to US national security. The company also said it acts on information received from US authorities about parties or organisations of concern.

Trump backs Huang

US President Donald Trump defended Huang on Sunday, praising his leadership and indicating that the controversy would not necessarily affect their working relationship. Speaking to reporters before returning to the White House, Trump said Huang had done an exceptional job and indicated he remained open to taking the Nvidia chief on an upcoming trip to Asia. Huang serves on the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, declined to comment on the allegations, citing the nature of the matter and Nvidia's internal investigation.

Why the investigation matters

The controversy comes at a sensitive time for Nvidia, which has become one of the most influential companies in the global AI industry. Its graphics processing units power the infrastructure used to develop and deploy advanced AI models. The company's dominance has also placed it at the centre of US-China technology tensions, particularly as Washington restricts exports of advanced chips to China.

The investigation presents Nvidia with questions extending beyond Huang's personal conduct, including the adequacy of corporate safeguards and whether intelligence concerns warrant changes to how senior executives engage with customers and business partners. For now, Nvidia's board has expressed confidence in Huang's continued leadership. Whether the investigation identifies any security lapses, and whether those findings lead to further corporate action, remains to be seen.

item.title: Vast, varied, vivid: How this art festival celebrates pan-India creativity
item.description: In this photo essay, we feature more highlights from Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath’s national art festival.
item.content:encoded:
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,030 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.

The Namma Art Bengaluru national festival was held at Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath (KCP) for the second time this year (see our coverage of earlier exhibitions at this popular cultural hub here). KCP’s flagship event is the annual Chitra Santhe, regarded as India’s largest street fair for art.

India’s artistic landscape is as vast and varied as the country itself. It spans intricate visual languages of Madhubani, Warli, Gond and Pattachitra; sculptural traditions of Channapatna, Dhokra and Thanjavur; miniature painting and textile traditions, and much more.

The worlds of contemporary painting, photography, installation, and new media add new perspectives and vocabularies for art lovers. The beauty of this artistic panorama truly emerges when these creative forms are showcased together.

“Art has always served as a powerful medium of expression that transcends boundaries, connects communities, and reflects the spirit of society,” explains Shashidhara Rao, General Secretary, KCP.

A pan-India exhibition that brings traditional and contemporary art into one shared space can create a powerful visual and cultural conversation. Instead of presenting India’s art traditions as isolated regional categories, such an exhibition reveals the connections between them.

Also Read
2026 Outlook: AI, robotics, biotech, unicorns and the road ahead

As seen in this photo essay, there are recurring ideas of nature, spirituality, community, identity, mythology, and everyday life. The differences are equally important: they demonstrate the extraordinary plurality of Indian experience and the many ways in which communities have interpreted and expressed their worlds.

Bringing traditional and contemporary practices together also allows the exhibition to move beyond the idea of heritage as something belonging only to the past. Traditional art forms are living practices, continually evolving through artists, artisans and new generations.

Contemporary artists, meanwhile, frequently draw upon inherited visual languages and stories while questioning, reinterpreting and transforming them for the present. Placing these works side by side makes this continuity visible.

“In an increasingly dynamic world, the role of art in preserving heritage, encouraging dialogue, and inspiring fresh perspectives has become more significant than ever,” KCP’s Rao adds.

The Namma Art festival is thus more than a showcase of beautiful objects, as shown in this photo essay. It serves as a map of India’s cultural imagination — one in which a folk painting from one region can resonate with a contemporary installation from another, and where regional identities can coexist within a larger national story.

The experience of seeing many art forms together is also deeply democratic. It invites audiences to discover unfamiliar traditions and appreciate the knowledge embedded in craft. It creates opportunities for dialogue between artists, craftspeople, designers, collectors, students, and the wider public.

Also Read
Year in review: startups that raised big from VCs in 2025

“Our festival represents a wide spectrum of artistic approaches, mediums and regional sensibilities. Their works collectively reflect the dynamism of contemporary practice in India,” says KCP president BL Shankar.

Such a national exhibition celebrates an idea that is central to India itself: unity does not require uniformity. Its strength lies in the coexistence of many languages, histories, materials, communities and ways of seeing.

By bringing traditional and contemporary art together, the exhibition can offer audiences not simply a view of Indian art, but an experience of India — diverse, layered, evolving, and connected.

Featured artists at the KCP festival include Vivek Vadkar, AG Nellagi, Ashok Mansur, Sunil Barman, Dhiraj Balchandra Patil, and Sudha Sridhar.

Vivek Vadkar is a contemporary Indian artist renowned for his powerful and emotive oil paintings of horses in motion. His popular Seven Horses compositions draw on traditions where running horses symbolise success, victory and positive energy.

AG Nellagi is known particularly for his expressive paintings of bulls. His work draws deeply on his personal experience as a farmer and on the cultural symbolism associated with the bull, which represents strength, determination, fertility, and confidence. He has received awards and recognition from the Karnataka Lalit Kala Academy and other cultural institutions.

Also Read
How IIT Madras Incubation Cell is powering India’s next-gen deeptech startups

Ashok Mansur is a visual artist and photographer with an interest in art, history and cultural imagery. A farmer by profession, he is also known for his beautiful landscapes along with people portraits.

Sunil Barman is a self-taught artist whose paintings focus on the quiet beauty of village life in Bengal. He works primarily with fine pen-and-ink drawing layered over delicate watercolour washes. His paintings evoke nostalgia for rural life where people and nature coexist in an unhurried rhythm.

“This edition has proudly presented 150 invited artists from across India. They showcase the diverse ideas, mediums and voices that reflect the spirit of traditional and contemporary art today,” festival convener SA Vimalanathan signs off.

Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?

(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath.)

item.title: Mamaearth parent’s profit surges 87%; Goyal defends Temple amid backlash
item.description: Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, registered an 87% YoY rise in net profit for Q2FY27, while revenue rose 36%. In other news, Deepinder Goyal has posted a series of updates on X amid backlash from some Indian doctors who criticised his wearable device Temple.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Readers, 

AI is finding cyber flaws swiftly. But are enterprises quick enough to fix them?

Nikesh Arora, Chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, raises this crucial point. He notes in a LinkedIn post that most organisations, especially the smaller ones, do not have the capacity to patch flaws at the speed needed. Arora advocates virtual patching as an interim measure and calls for a shared vulnerability clearing house and faster development of protective signatures. 

As AI agents become capable of handling everyday tasks, here’s a smart ring that promises to bring AI agents to our fingertips. 

At a private launch in Bengaluru, Aina unveiled an AI-powered ring that combines a colour display, voice commands, and gesture-based controls. The startup wants its device to become an everyday interface between users and AI agents. But can it offer enough utility to justify its Rs 47,000 price tag? 

In other news, the government has cleared 12 proposals worth over Rs 7,500 crore under the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme. This round of approvals adds to the momentum behind the scheme, which aims to build a domestic ecosystem for components and reduce India’s dependence on imports.

Meanwhile, MakeMyTrip has acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru-based Quick Ride, a tech-led shared mobility platform. Quick Ride connects people travelling along similar routes, enabling affordable ride pooling for everyday commute. 

Lastly, here’s a bit of weekend motivation. 

Built despite opposition, legal challenges, and questions over cost, Bihar Museum has marched into the global top 10, ahead of the Met and Louvre. For YourStory’s founder Shradha Sharma, the museum not only brings the region’s history to life, but is also a reminder of what ambition and perseverance can accomplish.

In today’s newsletter: 

  • Mamaearth parent Honasa’s net profit rises 87% 
  • Goyal defends Temple amid backlash

Here’s your trivia for today: Which company introduced commercially the first widespread videocassette in 1971?

Note: Starting this week, YS Buzz will land in your inbox Monday through Saturday. On Sundays, you'll continue to receive our Weekly Wrap, bringing together the biggest startup and business stories of the week. Thank you for reading YourStory and being part of our community.


Earnings 

Mamaearth parent Honasa’s Q2 net profit rises 87% 

Honasa Consumer, the parent company of beauty & personal care brand Mamaearth, registered an 87% year-on-year (YoY) rise in net profit for the second quarter of the current fiscal, while revenue rose 36% driven by strong growth across categories.

According to Honasa Consumer, the second quarter revenue growth is the highest it has recorded since its public listing in November 2023.

Key takeaways

  • The company’s net profit in Q2FY27 was Rs 73.24 crore, compared with Rs 39.22 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue was Rs 731.18 crore, compared with Rs 538.06 crore a year ago.
  • However, sequentially, profit fell from Rs 90.44 crore in the first quarter. Revenue in the first quarter was Rs 755.94 crore.
  • For the six months of the fiscal year, the company reported a revenue of Rs 1,487.13 crore, a YoY growth of 31%. The net profit for the period was Rs 163.69 crore, a YoY rise of 103%.

<Top Funding Deals of the Week>

Startup: GIVA 

Amount: $100M

Round: Undisclosed

Startup: EloElo Group 

Amount: $80M 

Round: Series C

Startup: Clinics On Cloud 

Amount: $12.5M

Round: Series A

Wearables

Goyal defends Temple amid backlash

Deepinder Goyal has posted a series of updates and clarifications on X amid backlash from some Indian doctors who criticised his brain-monitoring wearable Temple. Describing Temple as “an ambitious project”, Goyal gave a detailed explanation on what the team is building. “The team is delusional enough to think we can build this. And we will,” he wrote on Friday. 

Earlier, on Thursday, he posted, “We stand by our science and our methods. Each of our claims is easily verifiable by individuals and institutions alike, and you will see a lot of independent studies come up on their own when the device becomes available to use.”

Key takeaways: 

  • “First and foremost, a business lesson: if Temple were a scam, and any of what we said weren’t true, people would know it in just a few days of using Temple,” Goyal wrote on Thursday. 
  • He also highlighted that $30 million was invested in building the device, including $20 million of his personal money. Calling Temple his purpose, he said it’s not about the money. “I have enough of it to last for generations. My incentives are fully aligned with getting the science right. I am not staking a reputation earned over 20 years on making a quick buck.”
  • However, some doctors were not convinced by Goyal’s response. On X, Dr Rishabh Jain responded saying Goyal had shared financial and personal sacrifices but no scientific evidence. “Stop calling legitimate scientific scrutiny 'rage'. You have responded to questions about medical accuracy with investment figures, return policies, personal reputation, and promises of future studies. None of these constitutes scientific validation.”

News & updates

  • First close: Northern Arc Investment Managers, the asset management arm of Northern Arc Capital, has marked the first close of its Northern Arc Diversified Debt Fund with commitments of more than Rs 400 crore from institutions, family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals, and high-net-worth individuals. 
  • Court verdict: A division bench of the Delhi High Court has dismissed an appeal by Unity Bank, upholding the interim protection granted to BharatPe's parent company RIPL (Resilient Innovations Private Limited) under the Shareholders’ Agreement and affirming the order of a single judge.
  • Apple’s investments: Alphabet built a stake worth nearly $548 million in longtime partner Qualcomm in the ​third quarter, giving a boost to the chipmaker’s efforts ‌to expand into data centres as the smartphone market sees one of the worst downturns, Reuters reported. The Google ​parent has also increased its position in Elon Musk’s ​SpaceX to about ​555 million shares from 551.2 ‌million ⁠earlier.

Which company introduced commercially the first widespread videocassette in 1971?

Answer: Sony

item.title: Startup ecosystem sees sharp rise VC inflow; Building a hemp ecosystem in Uttarakhand
item.description: Industry watchers expect that a post-US midterm slowdown in AI funding could work in favor of Indian startups.
item.content:encoded:
Happy Diwali,

Financial services firm Angel One has climbed to the position of India’s second-largest stockbroker by active client count, according to the latest National Stock Exchange (NSE) data.

By the end of October, the brokerage reported 69.98 lakh active investors, commanding a 14.97% share of the exchange's total 4.67 crore active client base.

Meanwhile, benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty edged lower during Sunday’s special Muhurat trading session as profit-taking halted a seven-day rally, snapping an eight-year Diwali winning streak.

The BSE Sensex dipped 28.62 points, or 0.04%, to settle at 80,999.40, with 16 of its constituents ending higher and 14 lower. During the special session on Diwali, it hit a high of 81,442.11, surging 414.09 points, or 0.51%, PTI reported.

In the world of technology, a new cybercrime ‘gold rush’ is emerging as more and more people use the internet. Per a BBC Future article, around two billion people are expected to come online for the first time by 2030, but this digital leap comes with serious risks. Rather than entering a simple web, these newcomers are stepping straight into sophisticated cybercrime traps powered by AI, automated scams, and localised fraud. 

As CrowdStrike’s Zeki Turedi notes, while the internet unlocks life-changing opportunities, today's digital landscape is far more complex and dangerous for first-time users than the one earlier generations navigated.

In today’s newsletter, we will talk about 

  • Startup ecosystem sees sharp rise VC inflow
  • Building a hemp ecosystem in Uttarakhand

Here’s your trivia for today: What iconic consumer luggage company was founded in 1971 by Dilip Piramal, named after a Roman goddess of victory? (Scroll down for answer)

Venture capital

Startup ecosystem sees sharp rise VC inflow

November began on a positive note for the Indian startup ecosystem with venture capital inflow seeing a sharp rise. In total, the amount was $263 million across 23 deals against $115 million raised a week ago. 

This week marked two notable milestones for the Indian startup ecosystem. Total weekly funding comfortably crossed the $200 million mark—rebounding after a four-week slump below that threshold. Simultaneously, jewellery brand GIVA snapped the ecosystem’s month-long megadeal drought with a $100 million round.

Key takeaways:

  • Industry watchers expect that a post-US midterm slowdown in AI funding could work in favor of Indian startups.
  • Consumer AI startup EloElo Group raised $80 million from Hornbill Capital, NBCUniversal, MIT Investment Co, Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures and Griffin Gaming Partners.
  • Peppermint Robotics raised Rs 100 crore (~$10.5 million) from pi Ventures, Crane Venture Partners and Asiana Fund.

Social impact

Building a hemp ecosystem in Uttarakhand

While pursuing a master’s in Social Entrepreneurship at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Pavitra Joshi decided to return to the mountains, determined to tackle regional challenges through enterprise. 

What began as a classroom project soon evolved into KumaonKhand, a social enterprise building a hemp-based ecosystem in Uttarakhand. In 2021, Joshi turned the initiative into a full-time venture alongside his mother, Sangeeta, and Anuj Sharma, founder and CEO of impact incubator Alsisar Impact.

Key takeaways:

  • KumaonKhand’s product range is largely focused on hemp seed and hemp fibre. From hemp seed, they process hemp seed oil, which is in high demand in the skincare and pharmaceutical industries.
  • The company uses hemp in its own skincare range: lip balms, face creams, moisturisers, and handmade, sulphate-free soaps. It also makes hemp protein powder that has 44 grams of protein per 100 grams, making it one of the best sources of vegan protein.
  • Built using hemp-based materials, KumaonKhand’s factory incorporates hemp plaster and leftover hemp stalks as construction material. The material, known as hempcrete, is also being developed into a pre-mix plaster combining hemp and lime.

News & updates

  • Binance hack: Days after Binance saw a massive heist of  $6.3 billion, the cryptocurrency exchange said that its finance chief Kaiser Ng is ​leaving the company to pursue another venture. Justin Yek, a longtime finance executive who was most recently vice-president of finance at Airwallex, is ​taking over as CFO.
  • Infra push: Adani Enterprises Ltd plans an annual capital expenditure of Rs 35,000 crore to Rs 40,000 crore over the next few years, positioning airports, data centres, and a planned PVC complex as its primary growth drivers amid a broader infrastructure push.

What you should watch out for

  • Analysts expect bullion to remain subdued next week, weighed down by geopolitical shifts in the US-Iran standoff, crude price swings, and upcoming inflation data shaping the interest rate path.
  • Noel N. Tata will step down as Director and Vice-Chairman of Titan Company Limited on November 12, 2026, upon turning 70, in compliance with the Tata Group’s retirement and governance guidelines, the company informed stock exchanges.

item.title: VibeCode30 2026: The 30 AI-built products to watch from India
item.description: From healthcare and education to housing, travel, and developer tools, YourStory's inaugural VibeCode30 spotlights 30 live products showing how AI is making software development accessible to a new generation of builders.
item.content:encoded:
The next generation of technology builders may not all be software engineers. They could be students, product managers, marketing professionals, small business owners or simply individuals who understand a problem well enough to solve it.

With AI-powered coding tools lowering the technical and financial barriers to software development, more people are turning ideas into working products without conventional development teams or large budgets.

Recognising this shift, YourStory launched VibeCode30, a new initiative presented by Hostinger, at the 17th edition of TechSparks 2026 in Bengaluru. The inaugural cohort celebrates 30 AI-native products built to solve real-world problems, from simplifying house hunting and improving financial literacy to supporting healthcare professionals and making everyday business operations more efficient.

Unlike traditional startup showcases, Vibecode30 focuses on products and their builders, whether they work independently or in small teams, with or without formal coding experience.

The inaugural edition received 207 applications from across the country, including smaller centres such as Ajmer, Silvassa, Sugauli, and Thoothukudi. The final 30 products represent 19 industries and 11 cities, reflecting the range of problems that AI-native builders are addressing. Importantly, every selected product had moved beyond the prototype stage and was accessible to real users.

The cohort demonstrates that while AI can accelerate software development, understanding the problem, validating the output, and improving the product remain essential. It also shows how smaller, highly specific problems can now become viable opportunities for innovation.

Meet the VibeCode30 2026 cohort:

AjmerAstro

Built by Himanshu Dadhich in Ajmer, AjmerAstro is an AI-powered astrology platform offering personalised Vedic and KP astrology guidance in English and Hindi, with a system that remembers previous conversations.

AlgoTrips

Delhi-based Tushar Garg built AlgoTrips, an AI travel planner that creates day-by-day itineraries with live pricing for flights, hotels, activities, and transfers, allowing users to plan and book trips.

Arena

Developed by Bengaluru-based Prathik Arunkumar and Arun Kumar, Arena helps schools manage house competitions through live leaderboards, digital scoring, and real-time updates.

Beet.Health

Built by Vatsl Goswami and Shivanshi Shukla,  Beet.Health helps nutrition clinics manage appointments, payments, and meal plans while enabling clients to track their progress through a mobile app and WhatsApp assistant.

Bengaluru.rent

Created by Bengaluru-based Harshit Anand, Bengaluru.rent is a free platform where tenants anonymously share rental prices and connect directly with property owners and prospective flatmates without brokers.

Benki.tech

Developed by Sonam Rao, Avinash Narsimah, and Kumaraswamy BV in Bengaluru, Benki.tech uses a simulated panel of customers to help businesses pressure test business ideas, marketing messages, and product offerings.

Bloom UPSC

Built by Bengaluru-based former banker Guru Sasidhar Pattem, Bloom UPSC provides civil services aspirants with study materials, practice questions, answer evaluation, and video lessons in English and Telugu.

Boolean Beyond

Coimbatore-based Boolean Beyond developed BeyondSave, a WhatsApp-based platform that enables local jewellery businesses to manage customer savings schemes, payments, and balances.

ElderNest

Bengaluru-based Shubham Jain created ElderNest to help families discover and compare senior care homes across India, with information on services, pricing and admission support.

Gold Investment Monitor

Created by Surendhran Sivalingam in Coimbatore, Gold Investment Monitor analyses 24 market signals and combines them into a single verdic to help Indian households assess whether to buy gold or wait.

Holt

Built by Bhubaneswar-based Debashis Nayak, Holt is an open-source memory tool for AI coding assistants that runs locally on a developer’s machine, helping them retain project context across sessions.

IndianCoffeeBeans.com

Hyderabad-based Abhishek Thrilok built IndianCoffeeBeans.com, a searchable directory tracking more than 90 Indian specialty coffee roasters and 1,200+ coffees.

Indiccore

Developed by Sahil Gulati and his team in Gurugram, Indiccore helps civil services aspirants analyse mock-test performance, identify weaknesses, and improve examination strategies.

Madhav.live

Built by Ashish Singh Shekhawat in Bengaluru, Madhav.live lets users talk to Krishna about everyday problems and receive guidance rooted in the Bhagavad Gita, in the language they are most comfortable with.

MagicSlides.app

Created by Bengaluru-based Sanskar Tiwari, MagicSlides instantly converts topics, documents, web links, and YouTube videos into presentations, supporting more than 100 languages.

Mira

Developed by Shagun Verma and Abhaya Trivedi in Mumbai, Mira is an AI voice assistant that helps short-term rental hosts handle guest enquiries and check property availability, giving small hosts the kind of front desk usually only hotels can afford. 

NextDoor.Company

Built by Sankalp Sinha in Bengaluru, NextDoor.Company helps jobseekers discover startups hiring nearby through a map-based platform with company and employment information.

Nomira

Created by Bengaluru-based Prernaa Agarwal, Nomira is a women-first travel platform combining safety information, offline maps, travel communities, and group trips.

Orbit Research

Developed by Silvassa-based student Aditya Singh, Orbit Research combines academic research tools into a single platform for discovering papers, checking references, preparing manuscripts, and creating presentations.

Penfight

Built by Amarjeet Sarma and his Bengaluru-based team, Penfight recreates the popular school desk pen-flicking game as an online multiplayer experience.

Pretend AI

Pune-based Kareena Rogers developed Pretend AI, an iPhone app that allows users to rehearse conversations with custom AI personas through realistic text exchanges.

RayAI

Created by Reshma Budhia and Swetha Sree Kannan at Chennai-based agency Toss The Coin, RayAI helps marketing teams create campaigns, content and design assets using shared brand knowledge and workflows.

Soma

Built by Gurugram-based Saurav Singhal, Soma brings together health reports, wearable data, nutrition, and fitness information to provide personalised health insights.

TofuBofu

Hyderabad-based Arnav Neil developed TofuBofu to help B2B companies measure and improve how often AI recommends them, as buyers increasingly turn to AI for product research and decision making. 

Vitfinity

Created by Bengaluru-based Pranay Reddy and his team, Vitfinity teaches financial literacy to school children through interactive simulations and a 180-lesson curriculum.

Voqalize

Built by Sripathi Krishnan and his Bengaluru-based team, Voqalize enables enterprises to integrate multilingual conversational voice AI into software applications.

Whitefield Womania

Developed by Rakshita Dwivedi and Abhishek Dwivedi in Bengaluru, Whitefield Womania is a digital directory connecting residents with women-led local businesses.

Youdemy

Created by Bengaluru-based Rohit Ranjan Singh, Youdemy organises free YouTube lectures into structured courses with learning streaks, points, and leaderboards.

Zespan

Built by Udupi-based Abhishek N, Zespan monitors AI agents operating in enterprise environments, identifies incorrect decisions and helps prevent recurring errors.

Zoku

Developed by Bengaluru-based Priyanshu Dangi, Zoku is a voice-first development application that allows software developers to manage multiple AI coding agents simultaneously.
